newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stabilises in dull late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stabilises in dull late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah stabilised against the dollar in late Tuesday trading after falling in the morning on comments by the central bank governor, dealers said.
They said the rate was little changed, with spot rupiah last quoted at 2,325.50/26.50 at 0900 GMT.
It opened at 2,323.50/25.00 and fell to a low of 2,327.30 in late morning on rupiah selling by U.S. investment houses and stop-loss covering, dealers said.
Dealers said central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono had said in the United States overnight that Bank Indonesia had no plans to widen its intervention band again for now.
One local bank dealer said some U.S. investment houses seemed to have entered the market and sparked off a wave of rupiah unloading after the comments.
The local bank dealer said the dollar purchases started in the spot market, forcing buyers to buy forward and sell spot to to finance the transactions.
"The market is slightly bullish on dollars. The trend could be sustained for a while as operators are not so concerned about liquidity early in the month," one European bank dealer said.
He said the dollar-rupiah rate was likely to range between 2,324.50 and 2,329.50 on Wednesday, but the local bank dealer expected a range of between 2,324.00 and 2,327.00.
The local bank dealer said the central bank governor's statement did not herald any changes on fundamentals and the yield offered by the rupiah remained unchanged.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,325.25/26.00 and 2,323.0/23.5, respectively.
The local bank dealer said short-dated swaps remained high which kept roll-over costs expensive for holding dollars.
Overnight swap was at 0.55/0.60 and tom/next at 0.60/0.65.
One U.S. bank dealer said earlier offshore operators were seen covering short dollar positions after comments by the governor, which suggested limited downside for the dollar.
Local operators said comments by the finance minister on a depreciation target on Sunday and the central bank governor's comment on the intervention band contained nothing new.

But apparently those comments seemed to have given reasons for operators to cover back and to anticipate upside potential for the dollar, which has been under continuous pressure since the band widening last month.
The governor's comments contained no surprise as the band was widened only on September 13, local dealers said.
The local bank dealer said swap buying caused longer-term swap rates to edge up.
One-month swap edged up to 17.50/18.00 from 17.25/18.25, two to 33.0/35.0 from 32.5/33.5, three to 50.0/51.0 from 49.25/50.25 and six to 99.0/100.0 from 98.0/100.0.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,316/2,508 and the conversion rate at 2,316/2,364 on Tuesday.
